first_impression.reaction: Sophie here. James and I are swapping the placeholder ring for the real stone, so I Googled this. The first line won me over straight away: it's not a jeweller trying to sell me a stone. I skimmed the takeaways, read cut, the report checks, the ethics bit and the overseas section properly, and skimmed clarity, carat and most of the fluorescence numbers.

journey.quote: Most advice on choosing a diamond is written by someone with a tray of stones to sell you.
journey.reaction: Exactly how I feel walking into a jeweller. Saying it straight up makes me trust the rest more.

journey.quote: Our view is simple. For a round brilliant, put cut first.
journey.reaction: Good, an actual opinion. That gives James and me somewhere to start instead of arguing about carats.

journey.section: Checking the report number on the lab's own site
journey.quote: Type the number in yourself, on the lab's own website, rather than following a link or QR code someone hands you.
journey.reaction: This is the most useful line on the page. It's what I'd tell a client. It's going straight onto our list.

journey.quote: In a GIA study of E, G, I and K colour stones, average observers saw no systematic effect, and strongly blue stones were seen as having better colour when viewed table up.
journey.reaction: By here I'm skimming. The conclusion, that it's usually fine so look at it in daylight, would've been enough for me.

journey.quote: So "Kimberley Process compliant" speaks to one specific problem.
journey.reaction: Honest. I'd have taken that phrase as a blanket ethical tick. That's a proper trade-off, not marketing.

journey.section: Declaring it on return to Australia
journey.quote: If you go over the allowance, duty and tax apply to all goods of that type, not just the amount above the limit.
journey.reaction: That's the sort of hidden cost I worry about. Glad someone spelled it out.

journey.section: Declaring it on return to Australia
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the current requirements with you before you travel, as these rules can change.
journey.reaction: Wait, do you help with the ring as well, or only if we're getting married with you? It comes out of nowhere in a customs section, and I can't tell what I'd actually be signing up for.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish
journey.reaction: Every planner says they're end to end. Nothing here tells me what that means for 80 guests, half of them flying in, or my grandparents getting from the airport.

unanswered_questions: Does a Wedded Advisor actually help with buying or carrying the ring, or only once you've booked a wedding?
What does 'plans venue, travel, vendors and payments' cover for guests: flights, transfers, older relatives?
Is there a real wedding, with venue and date, that I can look at?
would_share_with: James: the shortlist checklist and the report-check section, before we go back to the jeweller
Not our parents; this one is about the ring, not the wedding

cta_reaction.quote: talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad
cta_reaction.why: It's low pressure, which I like, but I came here for a diamond. I'd click through to destinations first, and I'd only enquire after reading a couple of planning posts and seeing a real wedding.

top_3_changes: Spell out what a Wedded Advisor does around the ring (if anything), or move that line, so it doesn't read as a hint I can't follow up on.
Back up 'single point of contact from start to finish' with one concrete example, ideally a real wedding with venue and date, or one line on guest travel.
Trim the fluorescence statistics to the practical takeaway; the brand's voice is strongest in the plain-English 'do this before money moves' lines.

checks.check: Every journey point and the CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, 14 months out, wary of 'end-to-end' claims)
No invented brand facts; gaps listed in unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible
No invented problems; no hard turn-offs found

assumptions: Assumed the couple is engaged with a placeholder ring and choosing the final stone, consistent with being 14 months out from the wedding.
